picks.alt: The Crab Nebula: a tangled orange and blue cloud of filaments around a bright core, in a Hubble mosaic.
picks.note: A Hubble composite: neutral oxygen mapped to blue, sulfur to green, doubly ionized oxygen to red, not colours the eye would see.

picks.alt: The Lagoon Nebula: a wide pink and red cloud of glowing gas crossed by dark lanes, from the VLT Survey Telescope.
The Hercules globular cluster: a dense round swarm of hundreds of thousands of stars, brightest at the centre.
The Andromeda Galaxy: a tilted spiral with a yellow core, blue outer arms and dark dust lanes, with two small companion galaxies.
The Orion Nebula: a bright teal and red cloud of gas around the Trapezium stars, in a Hubble mosaic.
picks.note: A composite of visible and near-infrared filters plus an H-alpha filter, not a single visible-light exposure.

picks.alt: The Beehive Cluster: a loose scatter of bright white and yellow stars against a dark field.
The Pleiades: seven bright blue stars wrapped in wispy blue reflection nebulosity.
The Whirlpool Galaxy: a face-on spiral with pink star-forming knots along its arms, joined to a small yellow companion galaxy, from Hubble.

picks.file: File:Webb captures detailed beauty of Ring Nebula (NIRCam image) (weic2320b).jpg
picks.alt: The Ring Nebula seen by Webb's NIRCam: a glowing ring of gas with a faint star at its centre.
picks.note: Webb's near-infrared view, not a visible-light photograph.

picks.alt: M87: a smooth, round elliptical galaxy with a straight jet of plasma pointing out from its core, from Hubble.
picks.note: A composite of visible and infrared observations made to resolve the jet, not a single visible-light photograph.

picks.alt: Sagittarius A*: the Event Horizon Telescope's orange ring of light around the dark shadow of the black hole.
picks.note: A radio image from the Event Horizon Telescope, not a photograph in visible light.

picks.alt: The Hubble Deep Field: hundreds of faint galaxies of every shape and colour scattered across a tiny patch of dark sky.
The Eagle Nebula: dark pillars of dust rising into a red glowing cloud, from ESO's La Silla observatory.
The Trifid Nebula: a pink emission cloud split by three dark lanes, beside a blue reflection nebula, from the Rubin Observatory.
The Dumbbell Nebula: a round green shell of gas with pink edges, crossed by a scatter of foreground stars, from NOIRLab.

picks.file: File:VST snaps a very detailed view of the Triangulum Galaxy.jpg
picks.alt: The Triangulum Galaxy: a loose face-on spiral with a bright white core and red star-forming regions, from the VLT Survey Telescope.
picks.note: A composite that adds a narrowband H-alpha filter to broadband colour, so its red gas clouds read brighter than true colour.

picks.alt: M78: two bright blue reflection nebulae lit by young stars, with dark dust clouds around them, from ESO.
picks.note: A composite that adds a narrowband hydrogen filter to broadband colour, so its red gas glows brighter than true colour.

picks.alt: Bode's Galaxy: a grand-design spiral with a yellow core and blue arms, from Hubble.
The Cigar Galaxy: an edge-on disk with red filaments of gas blown out above and below it, from Hubble.
picks.note: A composite of visible, infrared and hydrogen-emission filters, not a single visible-light exposure.

picks.alt: The Sombrero Galaxy: a bright bulge with a dark dust ring seen almost edge-on, from Hubble.

picks.file: File:Nebulosa testa di cavallo con SPECULOOS.jpg
picks.alt: The Horsehead Nebula: a dark horse-head-shaped cloud silhouetted against a red glowing background, from ESO's SPECULOOS telescopes.
The Flame Nebula: an orange glowing cloud cut by a dark lane of dust, beside a bright star.
The Double Cluster: two dense groups of bright blue-white stars side by side.
The Double Cluster: two neighbouring clusters of blue-white stars in one wide field.
The North America Nebula: a red emission cloud shaped like the continent, with the Pelican Nebula beside it.
The western Veil Nebula: thin red and blue filaments of a supernova remnant, from the WIYN 0.9-metre telescope.
picks.note: A narrowband composite: hydrogen mapped to red, oxygen to blue, sulfur to green, not colours the eye would see.

picks.alt: The eastern Veil Nebula: bright braided filaments of red and blue-green gas, from the WIYN 0.9-metre telescope.
picks.note: A narrowband composite: oxygen mapped to blue, sulfur to green, hydrogen to orange, not colours the eye would see.

picks.alt: The Milky Way's band arching over ESO's Very Large Telescope, with a laser guide star pointed at the galactic centre.
Mercury: a grey, heavily cratered planet in true colour from MESSENGER.
picks.note: A composite of three narrow-band filters assigned to blue, green and red, MESSENGER's own approximation of true colour.

picks.alt: Venus: a pale yellow-white globe of unbroken cloud, from Mariner 10.

picks.file: File:Mars - August 30 2021 - Flickr - Kevin M. Gill.png
picks.alt: Mars: a rust-red planet with a white polar cap and dark surface markings.
Jupiter: banded cream and brown clouds with the Great Red Spot, from Hubble's 2024 OPAL programme.

picks.file: File:Saturn global view from Cassini, rings open Better Colour square crop.png
picks.alt: Saturn: the pale gold planet with its rings wide open, from Cassini.
The full Moon: grey maria and bright highlands with rays from Tycho crater.
picks.note: Shown full; the chart draws the phase for your moment.
